title: Block close: the voices
hook: a burning coal, a potter, dry bones, a sulking prophet, a donkey king

segments.voice: Yesterday, semeron, today, and the two ways Christians read the prophets. Your line was today it is fulfilled.

Isaiah's lips are still stinging from a burning coal. Jeremiah, who said he was too young, has clay from the potter's house on his sleeves. Ezekiel has heard dry bones rattle together in a valley. Daniel is fresh from the lions. Amos is still in his herdsman's clothes. Jonah is in a corner, sulking. Hosea is talking about his children. Zechariah is describing a king on a donkey. Habakkuk argued with God and came down singing. All in one room: loud, strange, brave, often unwelcome. Today, before the page turns, hear them all together.

The Hebrew word for prophet is navi, and the Bible shows the job. When Moses protests he can't speak well, God makes his brother Aaron his prophet, to say what Moses gives him. Not a fortune teller. A spokesperson. What did they say? To kings: you're not above the law. To festival crowds: your songs are noise while the poor are sold for a pair of shoes. To exiles in Babylon: comfort, you are mine, I have carved your name on my palms. To a people in rubble: a bag with holes, and build. To the hopeless: these bones can live; your old men shall dream dreams. Two notes, over and over: warning and comfort, justice and hope. Several pushed back on the job, like Moses. Jeremiah said he was only a child. Jonah paid his fare on a ship going the other way. Amos told a priest he was no prophet, just a herdsman taken from following the flock. Isaiah says here am I, send me, but only after a coal has touched his lips. They spoke anyway. Jeremiah said that when he tried to keep quiet, the word was like a fire shut up in his bones. Christians hear the prophets pointing forward to Jesus, who read their scroll in Nazareth and said today. Some also hear them pointing outward, to every place where a hard truth still needs saying. Tomorrow Luke's Gospel begins, with voices that sound like the prophets.
screen: `A FIRE SHUT UP IN THE BONES.`
then, large: `SOMEONE HAS TO SAY IT.`

segments.voice: Let the prophets' lines drift past: here am I, send me; comfort ye my people; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; I have called thee by thy name; let judgment run down as waters; do justly, love mercy, walk humbly; grace, grace unto it; yet I will rejoice; the weeping prophet's question. Keep the one that lingers, and say it slowly until you know it by heart. If you pray, offer it back to God; if not, simply keep it.
Navi, Hebrew for prophet, a spokesperson for God: often reluctant messengers with two notes, warning and comfort, justice and hope.
Your line: someone has to say it. A true thing, said gently and clearly. That's the prophets, done.

howItsDone: Christians read the prophets throughout the church year, especially in Advent and Lent, and many people keep a single line from them, on a card, a wall or in memory, as a word to live by.

fork.setup: you're Jeremiah. you've been given a hard, true word for powerful people, and you've decided not to say it. what happens?
options: you keep quiet and feel at peace.
the word burns in you until you speak.
you hand it to someone else.
fork.reveal: Jeremiah said the word was like a fire shut up in his bones; he couldn't hold it in, so he spoke.

original.note: Hebrew: prophet. in Exodus 7:1, Aaron is called Moses' prophet: the one who speaks for him.

trapdoor: what you thought: prophets were fortune tellers.
what it means: they were spokespeople, some of them reluctant, who carried two notes to their own day: warning and comfort, justice and hope.
what a scholar hears: Exodus 7:1 calls Aaron Moses' navi, the one who speaks for him: a picture of the word from inside the Bible itself.

chat.says: Weren't the prophets mostly fortune tellers, predicting what would happen?
options: Mostly spokespeople: they carried God's warning and comfort to their own day.
Yes, mostly; they read signs in the stars to predict what was coming.
They were mostly royal advisors who told kings what they wanted to hear.
chat.meaning: Navi means a spokesperson, like Aaron for Moses. The prophets carried two notes to their own day: warning and comfort, justice and hope.

navi.meaning: Hebrew for prophet, a spokesperson for God

Aaron.meaning: Moses' brother, who spoke for him

Ezekiel.meaning: the prophet who saw a valley of dry bones

Habakkuk.meaning: a prophet who argued with God, then sang

Babylon.meaning: the empire where Judah's people lived in exile
